112.title: Docs: reconcile PROMPT merging and Wave 0 with the delivered current-main protocol
112.body:
Closes #106

The orchestration merge checklist still described the pre-#105 procedure. This reconciles its merging and Wave 0 instructions with the delivered [merge-readiness protocol](https://github.com/Jev-Engineering/cookbook/blob/main/docs/merge-readiness.md) and directly cites the [standing ruling](https://github.com/Jev-Engineering/cookbook/issues/80#issuecomment-6031026593).

Signed current-main integration remains mandatory for recipes and material foundation advances. The narrow foundation-only immaterial ruling requires exact-main delta evidence, explicit same-head acceptance by every required genuine reviewer, complete current head/main checks, and unchanged helper NOT READY receipts. Missing evidence means material; any further main advance requires renewed assessment. Exact postmerge CI must finish before the next merge. The pinned squash command excludes branch deletion; cleanup follows verified delivery and owner confirmation.

Only orchestration/PROMPT.md changes. Manifest, review gates, recipe allowlist, cumulative live terms, and human release-tag gate are unchanged. All three commits are SSH signed and GitHub verified. All five actual checks pass on final head2fd09de8041a65e781731d32f317b37b860f2f15 and currentmain81cad07. Local pinned Ruff, catalog and hygiene checks pass; full supported-version baselines ran earlier, while the final prose revisions have hosted3.10/3.14 test coverage. Earlier local first-run failures remain unexplained and tracked by #109/#110, not attributed to load as fact.

Independent genuine Opus5.5 [final-head review](https://github.com/Jev-Engineering/cookbook/pull/112#issuecomment-6033795930) addresses the supervisor's [review](https://github.com/Jev-Engineering/cookbook/pull/112#issuecomment-6033678185) and [complete adjudication](https://github.com/Jev-Engineering/cookbook/pull/112#issuecomment-6033685802). The original supervisor's own fresh review and sole serial merge remain required. #113 tracks correcting the linked guide's pending-#106 status after delivery.

185.title: Foundation: evaluation helpers for multi-label pooling, outcome curves, ranking and fallback metrics (#161)
185.body:
Closes #161

## What this adds

`jev_cookbook.evaluation` gains the seven deliverables the issue's scope-consolidation comment (2026-10-09) lists, plus the matching docs and hygiene change. Base SHA after merging `origin/main` into this branch: `89bdd1a30207a23fc0349ef0795cc13243fe7fdf` (merge commit `499691caea0aab629fc13f6cc96ac59100567883`).

1. **Multi-label pooling + outcome tally.** `pool_label_decisions` (pools (example, label) decisions into flat `correct`/`confidence` arrays with label attribution kept) and `pool_label_outcomes` (a multi-label outcomes tally compatible with `evaluate_outcomes`) — `src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py:740` and `:808`. Tested in `tests/test_evaluation.py` by `test_pool_label_decisions_matches_the_hand_rolled_pooling_reference` (identity check against recipe 06's hand-rolled `pooled_correct_and_confidence`), `test_pool_label_decisions_single_threshold_for_every_label`, `test_pool_label_decisions_errors`, `test_pool_label_outcomes_matches_the_hand_rolled_tally_reference` (identity check against recipe 06's `tally_outcomes`), `test_pool_label_outcomes_matches_at_a_second_cutoff_with_some_uncertain`, `test_pool_label_outcomes_errors`.
2. **Hygiene generic username `agent`.** `tools/check_hygiene.py` `_GENERIC_USERNAMES` gains `agent` (this container's own account name) and sibling common words, without weakening the rule for real usernames. Tested in `tests/test_check_hygiene_generic_usernames.py`: `test_new_names_are_in_the_generic_set_and_pass_the_minimum_length`, `test_generic_username_list_still_excludes_short_words_by_length_alone`, `test_local_usernames_filters_out_each_new_name`, `test_new_generic_account_names_are_never_checked_by_name`, `test_no_account_name_means_the_name_check_stays_off_too`, `test_a_real_username_is_still_flagged_when_agent_is_also_a_reported_name` (real username still caught), `test_a_name_merely_containing_a_new_generic_word_is_still_a_real_checkable_username`.
3. **`noul_confidence` 1-ULP docs note.** `docs/evaluation.md` (around line 104) documents that hand-written mirror-probability literals such as `0.42`/`0.58` differ from `1 - p` by 1 ULP in floating point, so `noul_confidence` can yield two adjacent threshold candidates instead of one; the code fix is out of scope here (tracked separately as #172). No test — this is a documentation-only deliverable.
4. **Ranking: `mean_recall_at_budget` and `top_k_query_accuracy`, with the divergence test.** `src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py:1202` and `:1255`. `mean_recall_at_budget` is the thin mean of `recall_at_budget` over queries; `top_k_query_accuracy` is top-k ranking accuracy (is a relevant item among the top k) — the two diverge whenever a query has more than one relevant item, which is exactly the mistake recipe 17's local `top1_accuracy` made (it was `mean_recall_at_budget` under `top_k_query_accuracy`'s name). Tested by `test_mean_recall_at_budget_is_the_thin_mean`, `test_mean_recall_at_budget_skips_undefined_queries`, `test_top_k_query_accuracy_credits_a_clear_winner`, `test_top_k_query_accuracy_averages_over_queries`, `test_top_k_query_accuracy_gives_fractional_credit_on_a_tie_at_the_top`, `test_top_k_query_accuracy_diverges_from_mean_recall_at_budget_with_two_relevant_items` (the divergence test), `test_top_k_query_accuracy_agrees_with_mean_recall_at_budget_for_single_relevant_item`, `test_top_k_query_accuracy_is_one_when_every_item_is_relevant`, `test_top_k_query_accuracy_undefined_when_no_query_has_a_relevant_item`, `test_top_k_query_accuracy_errors`.
5. **`outcome_curve(confidences, accepted, correct)`.** `src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py:1528`, the `evaluate_outcomes` companion to `selective_curve`, returning the same `SelectiveCurve` row shape so recipes whose rule has a non-confidence review branch (04, 08, 11, 13, 14, 16, 21) can plot a risk-coverage curve that matches their own `evaluate_outcomes` numbers. Tested by `test_outcome_curve_equals_selective_curve_when_accepted_is_all_true`, `test_outcome_curve_uses_accepted_and_confidence_together`, `test_outcome_curve_is_nan_where_the_accepted_mask_selects_nothing`, `test_outcome_curve_rejects_out_of_range_confidence`, `test_outcome_curve_errors`.
6. **`set_agreement(gold_sets, choices)` and `fallback_metrics(gold_sets, choices, fallback)`.** `src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py:875` and `:899`. `set_agreement` is the share of choices inside an acceptable gold set (recipes 12 and 13's hand-rolled `choice in gold`); `fallback_metrics` is precision/recall/F1 of the fallback option via the two-class relabelling fallback recipes repeat. Tested by `test_set_agreement`, `test_fallback_metrics`, `test_fallback_metrics_accepts_choice_answers`, `test_fallback_metrics_degenerate_cases`.
7. **Docs: "Outcomes versus the confidence-only view".** `docs/evaluation.md` section "Outcomes versus the confidence-only view" (around line 297) states when `evaluate_selective`/`selective_curve` and `evaluate_outcomes`/`outcome_curve` coincide (a confidence-only review branch) and when they diverge (any additional non-confidence branch), and how to report the counterfactual for an exempted permissive option — recipe 16's lesson. This is a documentation-only deliverable; the behavior it describes is already covered by the pre-existing `test_evaluate_outcomes_matches_evaluate_selective_for_a_confidence_only_rule` and `test_evaluate_outcomes_diverges_from_evaluate_selective_with_a_second_review_branch` (not introduced by this PR).

Also from the issue body (items 2 and 4, folded into deliverables above): the "Noul three-path pattern" section states that a confidence-only review branch makes `evaluate_selective` and an outcome tally agree, and the "distance from 0.5, not margin at the threshold" warning (`docs/evaluation.md` line ~372) carries the per-label-threshold caveat for multi-label recipes.

**Explicitly out of scope** (per the scope-consolidation comment): the stable seeded-permutation helper was split out to #181 and has already landed on `main` via #184 (now in this branch through the merge, untouched by this PR); recipe-side migrations to use these helpers go to #163; the `noul_confidence` code fix (as opposed to the docs note) is #172.

## Decisions

- Function names and signatures follow the scope-consolidation comment verbatim (`outcome_curve(confidences, accepted, correct)`, `set_agreement(gold_sets, choices)`, `fallback_metrics(gold_sets, choices, fallback)`) rather than any alternative phrasing floated in earlier review comments on the issue.
- `pool_label_decisions` keeps per-label attribution by returning `(example_id, label)` keys alongside the pooled arrays, per acceptance criterion 1, rather than only the flat arrays.
- `outcome_curve` returns the same `SelectiveCurve` shape as `selective_curve` so existing plotting code that consumes one can consume the other unchanged.
- The wave-2 consistency-review follow-ups noted on the issue (S2 outcome-sweep caveats, S3 settling one `(accepted, correct)` parameter-order convention, S4 merging `false_merge_rate`/`false_link_rate`) are not addressed here — they were not part of the scope-consolidation comment's seven-item list and are left for a later pass.
- Local notebook execution was **not** run by this builder: two previous agents working this repository hung inside long-running shells executing `tools/execute_notebook.py` against scratch copies of other recipes. This PR touches no notebooks (`docs/evaluation.md`, `src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py`, `tools/check_hygiene.py`, and their tests only), so notebook execution is delegated entirely to CI's per-recipe `Notebook (<slug>)` jobs, which run every notebook on the PR head and diff it against the committed file.

## How it was verified

All commands run from this branch after merging `origin/main` (base `89bdd1a`), in a clean `uv`-managed venv, from the worktree root:

- `ruff check .` — all checks passed.
- `ruff format --check .` — 213 files already formatted.
- `python tools/check_hygiene.py` — passed, 307 files scanned.
- `python -m pytest -q tests/test_evaluation.py tests/test_check_hygiene_generic_usernames.py` — 175 passed, on both Python 3.14 (`.venv`) and Python 3.10 (`.venv310`).
- Full suite once, under the shared heavy-job slot, with `OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 MKL_NUM_THREADS=2 OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=2`: `nice -n 10 timeout 500 python -m pytest -q -x --no-header -p no:cacheprovider` — **2218 passed, 3 skipped in 97.45s**.
- Checked PR #183 (merged into `main` after this branch split off) made a single-option `Choice` raise: neither `tests/test_evaluation.py` nor `tests/test_check_hygiene_generic_usernames.py` constructs a `Choice`, so no test needed updating.
- `git diff origin/main...HEAD --name-only` (after the merge) lists exactly the five allowed paths: `docs/evaluation.md`, `src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py`, `tests/test_check_hygiene_generic_usernames.py`, `tests/test_evaluation.py`, `tools/check_hygiene.py`.

## Recipe checklist

Not applicable — this is foundation work (`src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py`, `docs/evaluation.md`, `tools/check_hygiene.py`, and their tests only; no recipe folder touched).

273.title: Foundation: pin a notebook's threshold-selection objective, not only its value (#244)
273.body:
Refs #244

## What this adds

#244 showed, three ways on recipe 38 (and independently on 39 and 36), that nothing pins a
notebook's threshold-selection **objective**: a keyword swap (`min_coverage=0.75` →
`target_accuracy=1.0`) can ship a byte-identical notebook whose printed `objective:` line is now
false, with the full suite, the recipe guard, and the notebook-freshness check all green. The two
things that look like pins are not: a hand-written printed f-string literal (nothing compares it
to the real call) and a test that only re-derives the resulting *value* (pins the objective only
if no other objective can reach that value on this recipe's own pool, which is exactly what has
not been checked, and which coincides on at least two published recipes' pools).

This PR does **items 1 and 4 of #244 only**, plus the allowlist bookkeeping that follows from
them. It deliberately does **not** do item 2 (the per-recipe mutation audit over 45 recipes) or
item 3 (fixing the drift) — see "What is not done" below for why, and whether I think item 2 is
subsumed.

**1. The guard** — `tests/test_recipe_guard.py`'s new `threshold_objective_pin` check (check 11).
For every real `select_confidence_threshold(`/`select_threshold(` call a recipe's committed
`notebook.ipynb` or `helpers.py` actually makes, the objective it selects (the keyword name for
the former; the objective string for the latter) must be asserted present somewhere in that
recipe's `tests/`, in a test that demonstrably reads the real committed source (a notebook cell's
`"source"`, or `inspect.getsource(helpers.<wrapper>)`/a raw read of `helpers.py`) — not a
hand-typed duplicate of it. Calls are found by walking the already-parsed `ast.Call` nodes, never
by a substring/paren-balance scan over cell text: a decorative `print(f"...select_confidence_
threshold(..., min_coverage=0.75)...")` is just a string constant in the AST, never an
`ast.Call`, so it cannot be mistaken for the real call the way a text scan can be (see "How it was
verified" for a mutation that demonstrates exactly this).

Two scope decisions beyond the issue's literal wording, both explained below: the check covers
`select_threshold` as well as `select_confidence_threshold` (the issue's own final comment widens
it there), and it requires the objective to be asserted *present*, not also every alternative
objective asserted *absent* — see "Decisions".

Also scans `helpers.py`, not only the notebook: three recipes (31, 35, and the general pattern the
template could fall into) route the selection call through a `helpers.py` wrapper the notebook
merely calls by name. Checking the notebook alone would silently *skip* those recipes rather than
reveal that they too lack the pin — the exact blind spot `G1(c)` already has for this shape (the
brief named it explicitly), which this check must not repeat.

**4. The template** — `docs/recipe-template.md` gains a new bullet ("Pin the threshold's
OBJECTIVE...") in the notebook-practices list, and a table-row update, both explaining the
property and pointing at the worked example. `recipes/_template/tests/test_helpers.py` gains
`test_the_notebook_selects_the_threshold_by_target_accuracy_not_min_coverage`, a working,
non-allowlisted pin on the template's own `python-rule` cell. A recipe built from the template and
adapting that test (the way `test_stored_answers_are_not_all_right` is already adapted per
recipe) gets a real pin, not an inert one.

**Allowlist bookkeeping** — running the new check against current `main` reveals **35 recipes**
with no such pin (full list below). Each is a new `(slug, "threshold_objective_pin")` entry in
`tests/recipe_guard_known_failures.py`, since I cannot touch any recipe's own files from this
branch. See "Decisions" for the reason-string convention I chose and why.

## The revealed list — 35 recipes (the remaining work)

```
01-sentiment-classification      14-source-span-selection          27-function-selection
02-refund-intent-detection        15-sensitive-text-triage          28-skill-selection
03-response-clarity-scoring       16-discord-moderation-triage      29-tool-outcome-verification
04-support-ticket-routing         17-passage-reranking               30-citation-verification
05-document-classification        18-duplicate-incident-matching    33-schema-field-mapping
06-multiple-topic-labels           19-ci-failure-classification      35-semantic-feature-extraction
07-word-sense-selection            20-claim-support-classification   41-approval-scope-review
08-faq-selection                   21-quiz-answer-adjudication        42-outbound-disclosure-screening
09-file-organization               22-cmdb-asset-matching             44-plan-constraint-assessment
10-answer-relevance-check          23-pairwise-answer-evaluation
11-clarification-selection         24-incident-priority-composition
12-thesaurus-word-selection        25-change-evidence-review
13-candidate-rewrite-selection     26-prompt-injection-screening
```

**10 recipes already pass** (31, 32, 34, 36, 37, 38, 39, 40, 43, 45), plus the template — these
already carry a working source-spelling pin and needed no allowlist entry. 31's and 35's calls
live in `helpers.py`; the rest are notebook-cell calls.

**31-patch-risk-triage and 35-semantic-feature-extraction** route the selection through a
`helpers.py` wrapper. 31 already has a working pin there (`inspect.getsource(helpers.choose_gate)`
+ `assert "min_coverage=" in source` + `assert "target_accuracy" not in source`); 35 has none (its
tests call the real wrapper for a *value* check only) and is in the allowlist.

## Decisions

- **`select_threshold` is in scope, not only `select_confidence_threshold`.** The issue's own
  final comment demonstrates the identical defect on `select_threshold`'s business threshold
  (recipe 39: `"f1"` → `"recall_at_precision", target=1.0"` returns the same value, printed label
  false, nothing notices) and asks for both functions explicitly. The detection mechanism and the
  property are the same either way, so I did not narrow to `select_confidence_threshold` alone —
  that would leave a documented, demonstrated instance of the same defect unguarded.
- **The check requires the objective present, not every alternative also asserted absent.** I
  considered requiring a negative assertion too (closing a theoretical "decorative duplicate"
  loophole), but the issue's own list of "what does work" names recipe 37 as a working example,
  and recipe 37's pin is positive-only (`assert 'objective="f1"' in cells[...]`, no negative
  anywhere). Requiring exhaustive negatives would reject an example the issue itself endorses, and
  — checked directly — even recipe 39's committed fix excludes only one of `select_threshold`'s two
  alternatives, not both. I matched the issue's own standard (keyword/value asserted present,
  tied to the real committed source) rather than inventing a stricter one unilaterally. The mutation
  proof below shows this is still sufficient to catch a real keyword swap, including the decorative
  duplicate case, because the check derives the objective from the real `ast.Call` independently of
  whatever decoration says.
- **Allowlist pooling is per-recipe, not per-call.** I checked (see "How it was verified") that no
  currently-published recipe mixes objectives across two calls to the same function (e.g.
  `min_coverage` in one `select_confidence_threshold` call and `target_accuracy` in another), so
  pooling every asserted-present spelling across a recipe's test files cannot let one call's real
  pin stand in for a different call's missing one, for any recipe that exists today. This is a
  scope simplification I am disclosing rather than one I verified is permanently safe: a future
  recipe that did mix objectives within one function could, in principle, defeat this pooling, and
  a later tightening (score per-call-site rather than per-recipe) is a reasonable follow-up, not
  required by #244's item 1.
- **Reason-string convention: `"... see #244"`, not `"... see #163"`.** The allowlist's own
  docstring says every entry "ends with `see #163`", and this was true of every entry until now
  because every prior stricter-check addition was still part of the #163/#165 sweep lineage. These
  35 entries are different: the drift this check reveals is **#244's own scope** (its acceptance
  criteria literally ask for a per-recipe audit of exactly this), and #163's sweep was closed out
  with an empty allowlist — it has no mandate over a check #163 never named. Citing `#163` on these
  would make `grep '#163'` falsely claim ownership of someone else's work list, and the orchestrator
  told me the remaining list in this body *is* the dispatch list for #244's own reviewed sweeps. So
  I generalized `tests/recipe_guard_known_failures.py`'s docstring (the rule is now "ends with
  `see #NNN`, the issue that owns clearing it", with #163's history kept as the default case) and
  removed the hardcoded `"#163: "` prefix `tests/test_recipe_guard.py::guarded` was adding to every
  xfail `reason=` regardless of what the allowlist actually said (harmless until now, since the
  allowlist was empty — no entry's displayed reason has ever depended on this). I believe this is
  the right call given the brief's own framing, but it is a convention decision, not purely
  mechanical, and I'm flagging it explicitly rather than treating it as obviously correct.

## What is not done, and whether the mutation audit is subsumed

**Item 2 (the per-recipe mutation audit)**: I agree it is **subsumed for the keyword-swap question**
specifically. The audit's stated purpose is "which recipes fail to pin the objective keyword" —
the guard answers exactly that, mechanically, for all 45 recipes at once, the moment it fails
closed, and the revealed list above *is* that answer: no notebook re-execution is needed to learn
it, because a source-spelling assertion is a static, syntactic fact about committed text, not
something that changes under re-execution.

**Where it is not subsumed**: the issue's final acceptance criterion also asks to record "any
recipe where the two objectives coincide on its pool (those are the ones where a value-only
assertion is most misleading)". That is a *numeric* property of a recipe's fixtures under
re-execution (do `min_coverage=X` and `target_accuracy=Y` select the same threshold on this
specific pool?), not a syntactic one, and this guard does not and cannot measure it — nor does it
need to, for the keyword-swap defect itself: if the test's pin is tied to the real **committed
source spelling** (as this check requires), the swap is caught regardless of whether the two
objectives happen to coincide on that recipe's data. Coincidence only matters for a *value-based*
pin, and the whole point of item 1's fix is to stop relying on one. So the coincidence-mapping
half of item 2 is real, separate, additional information (useful for understanding *how* a given
recipe's drift arose, and possibly useful context for whoever fixes it), but it is not required to
either build this guard or to know which recipes need fixing — that list is already complete
above by construction. I have not attempted to produce the coincidence map; it would need
re-executing each flagged recipe's notebook under both objectives, which is explicitly out of
scope for a foundation builder per `BUILDER_RULES.md`'s no-local-notebook-executions rule, and is
exactly the kind of per-recipe work the orchestrator said it would dispatch as reviewed sweeps.

**Item 3 (fixing the drift)** is explicitly not mine — `recipes/<slug>/` files are untouched by
this branch.

## Out-of-scope findings

- **G1(c)'s existing helpers.py blind spot (tracked, per Wave 3 brief rule 18, as a known,
  separately-tracked foundation issue) is the same shape this new check had to avoid**, and did:
  see "What this adds" above for how 31/35 are covered. I did not touch `G1(c)` itself.
- **#272** (the coordinator flagged this mid-task): `_find_function_body`'s next-def regex scan is
  unsound when the audited function is followed by a decorated one. My new check never uses that
  helper — it walks the whole file's `ast` and bounds each function with `ast.get_source_segment`,
  which is immune to the same class of bug — and I added one documentation sentence to
  `_test_function_defs` stating this explicitly, for a future reader wondering why. I did not fix
  #272 itself.
- **Recipe 28's `test_select_margin_threshold_uses_min_coverage_not_target_accuracy`** is a
  genuinely clever *value*-based discrimination test (it checks `by_min_coverage != by_target_
  accuracy` on this recipe's own pool before relying on equality with the real wrapper's result),
  which is sound reasoning for distinguishing the two objectives on that specific pool — but it is
  still a value-based mechanism, not the source-spelling property #244 asks for, so my check
  correctly does not credit it and 28 is in the allowlist. Worth knowing if a future #244 sweep on
  28 is tempted to argue the existing test already suffices.

## How it was verified

All commands run from `/workspace/worktrees/foundation-244`, Python 3.14 venv, `pip install -e
".[dev]"` (no `[ml]`: no notebook is executed by this branch's own checks).

```
ruff check .                                             # All checks passed!
ruff format --check .                                    # 352 files already formatted
pytest tests/test_recipe_guard.py -rX
  # 650 passed, 4 skipped, 45 deselected, 35 xfailed in ~4s   (0 xpassed)
pytest -rX                                                # bare root, CI's own invocation, [dev] extras
  # 4069 passed, 7 skipped, 45 deselected, 35 xfailed in 113.35s   (0 xpassed, 0 failed)
python tools/render_catalog.py --check                   # exit 0 (unpiped)
```

The bare `pytest -rX` was piped to `tail` to capture output within this message's budget; the
exit code I read immediately afterward is therefore the pipe's, not pytest's, and I am not citing
it as evidence. The summary line itself — "4069 passed, 7 skipped, 45 deselected, 35 xfailed",
with no `failed`/`error` term — is pytest's own authoritative aggregate over the whole run
regardless of exit code, and that is what I am relying on.

**Mutation proofs** (run directly against the guard's own functions, imported by file path, over
throwaway `shutil.copytree` copies under `/workspace/worktrees/_scratch/foundation-244/tmp`; every
copy was deleted afterward and the real `recipes/` tree was never touched):

1. **Fails closed on a notebook-side keyword swap, test untouched** (recipe 38, currently passing).
   Changed the committed `python-rule` cell's real call from `min_coverage=min_coverage` to
   `target_accuracy=target_accuracy` (asserted `mutated_text != original_text` before
   interpreting anything). Independently confirmed via `ast` that the real call's objective is now
   `target_accuracy`. The check's only assertion, `assert not violations`, fired with: `cell
   python-rule select_confidence_threshold(...): objective 'target_accuracy' is not asserted
   present` — the exact recipe, cell, and missing spelling.
2. **Fails closed on a misspelled/removed test-side assertion, notebook untouched** (recipe 38).
   Changed `assert "min_coverage=min_coverage" in source` to `assert "min_covverage=min_covverage"
   in source` (and the companion line), asserted the text actually changed, then re-ran. Same
   assertion fired: `cell python-rule select_confidence_threshold(...): objective 'min_coverage'
   is not asserted present`.
3. **Cannot be evaded by a decorative duplicate** (the exact #244 scenario). Built a mutated copy
   of recipe 38's cell where the real call is swapped to `target_accuracy`, but a hand-typed,
   non-interpolated decorative `print("...select_confidence_threshold(..., min_coverage=0.75)...")`
   is left behind — the original inert pattern. A naive whole-cell substring check
   (`"min_coverage" in cell_text`) returns `True` here: it would be fooled into reporting the
   recipe as still pinned. This guard's own `ast`-based extraction is not: it finds exactly one
   real `ast.Call`, correctly derives its objective as `target_accuracy` independent of the
   decoration, and the same assertion fires with the same message as in (1).

I did not re-execute any notebook for any of this (static source/AST analysis only), consistent
with `BUILDER_RULES.md`'s no-local-notebook-executions rule for foundation work.

**Cross-check that per-recipe allowlist pooling is safe today**: scanned every real
`select_confidence_threshold`/`select_threshold` call (notebook + `helpers.py`) across all 46
published recipes by `ast`; no recipe uses more than one objective for the same function (e.g. two
`select_confidence_threshold` calls with different keywords) — see "Decisions" above.

**Heavy-lock discipline**: acquired `/workspace/worktrees/_scratch/HEAVY.lock` in its own bounded
command (confirmed no stale lock, no process under any worktree beforehand), ran the full `pytest`
as the very next command, released with an ownership-checked `rm -rf` in the same command, no

280.title: Foundation: key the scripted-recipe guard skips on the property each check means, not responses.json
280.body:
Refs #249

Not all acceptance criteria are met as predicted by the issue — see "Decisions" and "Item 2" below for why `Refs` rather than `Closes` is correct here.

## What this adds

Three of the recipe guard's scripted-recipe skips were keyed on `fixtures/responses.json`'s existence, a correlate of "this recipe's answers are stored" rather than of what each check actually means. This re-keys two of the three skips on their real property, documents the third (which was already correctly keyed), and enumerates all three in the module docstring with individual reasons. Diff is `tests/test_recipe_guard.py` only — no recipe file, including the template, was touched.

### Item 1 — `G1(c)` (`stored_answers_strong_form`, line ~511)

**Property this check is now about:** does this recipe freeze a confidence or business threshold at all (a real `select_confidence_threshold(`/`select_threshold(` call somewhere in its committed notebook or `helpers.py`) — not whether its answers happen to be stored in `responses.json`.

The skip is now keyed on `_threshold_pin_obligations(recipe_dir(recipe))`, the same real-call detector `threshold_objective_pin` already uses (AST-level, walks the committed notebook cells and `helpers.py`, resolves import aliases) — reused rather than re-implemented, per the house guidance against enumerating spellings.

**Measured outcome — differs from the issue's prediction, and I want to flag that clearly rather than paper over it.** The issue states "with the skip removed, 36 recipes pass and recipe 36 alone fails" and expects an allowlist entry naming #249. I re-ran this exactly as described (skip removed entirely, then re-keyed) against the current published set (47 recipes + template) and recipe 36 **passes**, with 48/48 passing and 0 skipped. Tracing it down: PR #246's own fix round (comment "strong-form test name misses `G1(c)`'s anchor") renamed the test function from `test_scripted_answers_are_not_all_right_...` to `test_stored_answers_are_not_all_right_above_the_frozen_confidence_gate` *before merge*, specifically to satisfy `STRONG_FORM_DEF`'s substring match. The issue's "would FAIL" measurement was taken against an earlier revision of that PR, before its own fix round landed; the defect it names was already closed by the time recipe 36 reached `main`. **No allowlist entry is added** — adding one for a check that genuinely passes would itself be a hard failure under `tests/recipe_guard_known_failures.py`'s `strict=True` xfail (an unexpected pass raises `XPASS(strict)`), which is a decisive, mechanical confirmation that recipe 36 really does pass this check today, not just my own reading of the code.

**Proof the changed skip can both fire and not fire:**
- *Fires* (no threshold frozen): `test_stored_answers_strong_form_skip_fires_only_when_no_threshold_is_frozen` (new regression test, right after the parametrized check) — a throwaway `tmp_path` copy of recipe 36 with its one `select_confidence_threshold(` call and its import stripped; `_threshold_pin_obligations` returns `[]` on the mutated copy and is asserted non-empty on the unmodified copy first (so the mutation is proven to have taken, not merely assumed).
- *Does not fire* (threshold frozen, check runs for real): the parametrized case `test_stored_answers_are_not_all_right_is_the_strong_form[36-card-game-action-selection]`, which is PASSED (not SKIPPED) in every run above — the live, continuously-run proof for this direction.

### Item 2 — README live-call count (`readme_budget_note_matches_stored_answers`, line ~1159) — investigated, NOT implemented; reasoned deferral

The issue's own suggestion is to derive the README's stated live-call count from the notebook's actual `decide()` calls rather than from `len(responses.json)`, which would make the check apply to scripted recipes and close #213's gap (a doubly-decided example collapsing to one entry in a dict keyed by replay state).

**Investigation, and why I did not implement it:**

- `len(responses.json)` is already a proxy, not a direct count, even for non-scripted recipes: it counts *distinct decided states*, by construction of `build_fixtures.py`. Recipe 36's own numbers are the clean counterexample — 96 scored rows, 290 real `decide()` calls (measured by PR #246's reviewer via hand-instrumentation), only 72 distinct states. The proxy and the real count differ by 4x on data already in this repository.
- There is no committed artifact today, for any recipe, that holds the real `decide()`-call count. `ReplayBackend`/`ScriptedBackend` (`src/jev_cookbook/backends.py`) keep no call counter (`requests_made` exists only on `LiveBackend`, `src/jev_cookbook/live.py:587`). The only way to recover the true count is to execute the notebook's real control flow with a counting wrapper — which is literally what the PR #246 reviewer did by hand.
- **A static route (fixtures row count × call-sites, no execution) does not generalise.** It works for a simple "one call per row" recipe, but recipe 36's own count is a function of card-game simulation dynamics (episode length varies by game state) — not a closed form over `inputs.jsonl`'s row count. This is the same shape of trap as the Wave-3 brief's rule 19 "never let a formula be the derivation" and rule 16's four-times-corrected quantity confusion (rows vs. requests vs. questions vs. units): a formula that fits today's simple recipes breaks on the next irregular one, silently, which is exactly the "a check keyed on a shape rather than a property" failure #249 itself exists to stop.
- **A "committed-output" route** (read an already-executed, already-committed count from a notebook cell, the way `measured_cell_prints_n_offline` reads a committed `N:` line, with no execution performed by the guard itself) would work in principle, but no currently published recipe's committed output carries such a counter — it would require (a) a shared counting-backend wrapper (fine, shared code) **and** (b) retrofitting every recipe's notebook to use and print it, which means editing and re-executing every one of 46+ recipes. That is squarely a recipe-files change and a cross-recipe sweep, both outside this foundation PR's permitted diff (`tests/` only, no recipe files) and outside this issue's scope.
- `#213` — the issue this gap is actually tracked under — already names the right fix location in its own body: *"instrumenting the backend during the offline execution CI already performs is the cheap route, since replay and live take the same path through `decide`"*. That is the per-recipe `Notebook (<slug>)` CI job, which already executes every notebook; adding a counting assertion there is close to free marginal cost. The shared `Tests` leg (where `tests/test_recipe_guard.py` runs) explicitly does not execute notebooks and should not start doing so for one check.

**Conclusion: this needs a different home — #213's own per-recipe `Notebook (<slug>)` CI job, not this guard's `Tests` leg.** I have not implemented a static or execution-based route here. What I did do, in scope: reworded the skip's docstring and message to name the real property ("no committed artifact this check can read a real call count from," not "no responses.json") and to point at #213 and #249 for the next reader, so the skip is at least honestly described rather than silently proxy-keyed. The acceptance criterion "the README live-call check applies to scripted recipes, **or a recorded decision explains why it cannot**" is met by the second half.

### Item 3 — `build_fixtures_scaffold` (line ~316) — left as a skip, docstring improved

**Property:** does this recipe's scaffold produce a `tests/test_build_fixtures.py` to hold byte-identical to anything. `tools/new_recipe.py --mode scripted` (`build_scripted_fixtures_text`) never writes `responses.json` and never writes that test file — genuinely vacuous for a scripted recipe, confirmed by reading `tools/new_recipe.py` directly rather than trusting the issue's characterization. Skip is unchanged in mechanism (still keyed on `responses.json`'s absence, which **is** the real property for this one check), but the function's own docstring and the skip message now say why, naming #249.

### Item 4 — module docstring

The `"... none are published yet"` line is gone (false the moment recipe 36 merged, which it already has). Replaced with an enumeration of all three scripted-recipe skips, each with its own property and reason — see the module docstring in the diff, right before the `from __future__ import annotations` line.

### Item 5 — full published set, each skip condition temporarily removed

Measured against the current published set (47 recipes + template; the only scripted recipe is 36 — confirmed by scanning every `recipes/*/fixtures/` for a missing `responses.json` beside a committed `notebook.ipynb`):

| check | skip lifted | result |
|---|---|---|
| `stored_answers_strong_form` (G1(c)) | entirely, then re-keyed on the property | **0 newly-failing recipes.** 48/48 pass either way. Recipe 36 passes (see item 1's measured-outcome note above). |
| `build_fixtures_scaffold` | entirely | **1 newly-failing recipe: `36-card-game-action-selection`** — `AssertionError: no tests/test_build_fixtures.py`. Expected and vacuous (item 3); not a defect, no allowlist entry (it's the correct, honest outcome of a check that doesn't apply, not drift to hide). |
| `readme_budget_note_matches_stored_answers` | entirely | **1 newly-failing recipe: `36-card-game-action-selection`** — crashes with `FileNotFoundError` on the missing `responses.json` once the skip is removed (not a clean `AssertionError`, which is itself evidence this check's current shape cannot be extended to a scripted recipe without the item-2 redesign). Expected and vacuous; not a defect, no allowlist entry. |

**No allowlist entries were added by this PR.** `tests/recipe_guard_known_failures.py` is unchanged (still 31 entries, diff is empty on that file) — every lifted skip either produces no new failure (item 1) or produces the already-understood, non-defect vacuous failure the issue itself labelled correct (items 2 and 3).

## Decisions a later builder/reviewer will have to live with

- **Item 1's allowlist expectation was not followed, on measured evidence contradicting it.** I verified this three ways: a direct Python probe calling the guard's own functions, the real parametrized pytest case (`PASSED`, not `SKIPPED`), and a from-scratch removal of the skip condition entirely (not just the re-keyed version) over the whole published set, all agreeing recipe 36 passes. I'm reporting this prominently rather than silently adding a speculative entry, per "never weaken a check" and the allowlist's own `strict=True` design, which would have rejected a fabricated entry anyway.
- **Item 2 is a deferral, not an implementation.** I changed only the skip's wording/documentation, not its mechanism. The right next step is on `#213`, in the per-recipe `Notebook (<slug>)` job, not here.
- **`_threshold_pin_obligations` is reused, not duplicated**, for item 1's skip condition — it is defined later in the same module (line ~1429 after this change) but that's a forward reference resolved at test-run time, not at class-body or import-ordering time, so it's safe; both call sites (the pre-existing `threshold_objective_pin` check and this skip) now agree on what "this recipe has a real threshold call" means, which is exactly the kind of one-definition-of-the-property discipline #249's general point asks for.
- **No recipe file was touched, including the template** — the template already has a confidence gate and `responses.json`, so it is unaffected by the item-1 re-keying either way; it was never skipped before and is not skipped now.

## How it was verified

All commands run from `/workspace/worktrees/foundation-249`, two clean venvs (`uv venv --python 3.14 .venv`, `uv venv --python 3.10 .venv310`, both `uv pip install -e ".[dev]"`, no `[ml]` — no notebook was executed locally).

```
source .venv/bin/activate
ruff check .                                   # All checks passed!
ruff format --check .                          # 364 files already formatted
python tools/render_catalog.py --check         # rc=0
[omitted; sha256: a0bc7aed93c870e85d60eb70de382fed5d375427721701eb75e9d818967fb7ac] python -m pytest tests/test_recipe_guard.py -rX -q
  # 690 passed, 3 skipped, 47 deselected, 31 xfailed
[omitted; sha256: a0bc7aed93c870e85d60eb70de382fed5d375427721701eb75e9d818967fb7ac] python -m pytest -q
  # 4287 passed, 6 skipped, 47 deselected, 31 xfailed   (bare pytest, CI's own invocation, py3.14)

source .venv310/bin/activate
[omitted; sha256: a0bc7aed93c870e85d60eb70de382fed5d375427721701eb75e9d818967fb7ac] python -m pytest -q
  # 4287 passed, 6 skipped, 47 deselected, 31 xfailed   (bare pytest, py3.10)
```

The 6 skips on both interpreters: 3 pre-existing and unrelated (`typesafe_sdk` not installed x2, `pre-commit`/environment ruff not installed), 1 pre-existing and unrelated (recipe 16's named `ESCALATE` exemption), and the 2 from items 2 and 3 above, both now worded to name the real reason and both pointing at #249/#213.

Both full-suite runs were the one heavy job per hold, in the canonical `/workspace/worktrees/_scratch/HEAVY.lock`, acquired in its own bounded command and released by an ownership-checked trap in the same command as the `pytest` call (not a separate acquire command — so the trap never fires before the heavy job it protects). Checked `/proc/*/cwd` across all worktrees before each acquire; nothing else was running either time. Both runs completed and the lock was released before this PR was opened.

## Recipe checklist

Not applicable — this is a foundation pull request; no recipe folder was touched.

## Out of scope — for the orchestrator, not for this branch

- **#213 itself** (the real fix for item 2) needs a design decision about where a counting wrapper lives in `src/jev_cookbook/backends.py` and how the per-recipe `Notebook (<slug>)` CI job would assert against it, plus a cross-recipe sweep to retrofit every notebook once that design is chosen. Not mine to do here.
- **The issue's own "would FAIL" measurement for item 1 was stale by the time this issue was filed** (PR #246's fix round had already renamed the anchor-missing function). Worth a note on #249 itself so a future reader doesn't re-derive the same surprise; I'm not editing the issue, just flagging it here per the house rule on reporting out-of-scope findings in the PR/report rather than only in a code comment.
- **`_find_function_body` (line 442) still has the #272 decorator-folding defect**: it scans forward by regex to the next `\n(?:def |class )` rather than using the parser's own `end_lineno`, so a decorated neighbour folds into the extracted body and `ast.parse` can raise a `SyntaxError` that blames the recipe rather than the extraction. Not touched here and not exercised by anything in this change (recipe 36's one match is a prefix match with no intervening decorator before the next `def`), confirmed by the new regression test passing.

292.title: Foundation: state Noul fixture requirements where issue authors and builders meet them
292.body:
Refs #283

Not all of #283's acceptance criteria are met by this branch alone -- see "Acceptance criteria" below. The PR body therefore says `Refs #283`, not `Closes #283`.

## What this adds

Recipe 48's review (feeding into #281) measured that a multi-proposition `Noul` issue can reach a builder with no requirement for a positive example of every proposition, no truth-combination coverage, and no row where a proposition's own tag changes the composed outcome -- because that requirement lived only in an orchestration brief, never in a file a repository reader can open. This closes that gap in the two places people actually read:

1. **`docs/recipe-template.md`**, at the existing `Noul` contract bullet -- the builder-facing document. States the three fixture-set requirements for a multi-proposition `Noul` recipe, with the reason each matters, in the document's own voice.
2. **`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/recipe.yml`**, the issue-author-facing form -- one added sentence in the existing "Fixtures and evaluation" field's description, prompting for the same three things when an issue proposes more than one `Noul` proposition together.
3. **`tests/test_recipe_guard.py`**, a new guard check, `noul_proposition_gold_coverage`: for every `Noul` proposition that zero-argument discovery reaches in a recipe's own code (discovered by calling the recipe's zero-argument question-building functions and keeping the `Noul`-valued entries of whatever dict each returns -- never by name or spelling), `labels.jsonl` must carry a gold-true row and a gold-false row for that proposition in every scored split. This is the mechanical half of #283's three requirements (the gold-coverage one); the truth-combination and outcome-determining requirements are not mechanically checked here -- see "Guard decision" below for why.

## Decisions

- **Scope of the guard.** #283 names three requirements; only the first ("at least one gold-true and one gold-false row per proposition per scored split") is stated as a candidate for a mechanical check in the issue itself. I implemented that one and investigated the other two (see "Guard decision"). I did not force the combination or outcome-determining properties into a guard that would have to key on something other than the real question definitions.
- **Discovery is by calling code, not by name.** `_noul_propositions` (tests/test_recipe_guard.py) calls every zero-required-argument function `helpers.py` defines (not one it imports) and keeps the `Noul`-valued entries of any dict it returns. This is the seventh time this repository has had to choose between an idiom-keyed check and a property-keyed one (#222, #227, #234, #270, #272, #276, #282 are the first six); I chose property-keyed. Measured: 51 such calls across 49 published recipes plus the template, 0 files opened, 0 output, 0 exceptions; the calls themselves take about 0.02s and the whole discovery sweep including module loads about 0.2s. Most calls are question builders, but not all: the docstring names the nine others that get called (e.g. recipe 36's `enumerate_game_space`). A recipe whose question builder takes an argument (recipe 39's `build_stage2_questions(which)`) is not reached and is skipped with a reason saying so.
- **Gold-value reading handles three shapes, not one.** Published multi-proposition `Noul` recipes record gold three different ways: a flat `{prop: bool}` mapping (26, 41, 42, 44, 48), one level of nesting (`{"features": {prop: bool}}`, recipe 35), and set-valued gold -- a list of the true proposition names (06, 37). `_noul_gold_value` reads all three. A fourth shape exists in the published set -- a bare `true`/`false` with no proposition key at all (recipes 02, 10, 15) -- but it occurs only when a recipe has exactly one `Noul` proposition, which this check does not apply to (see next point), so it is deliberately not read.
- **The check is scoped to two-or-more propositions, by skip, not by vacuous pass.** #283 is about the battery case. A recipe with 0 or 1 `Noul` proposition is `pytest.skip`-ed with a reason naming the count found, not silently passed.
- **No `tests/recipe_guard_known_failures.py` entry was needed.** All ten published multi-proposition `Noul` recipes the check reaches (06, 25, 26, 31, 35, 37, 41, 42, 44, 48) already satisfy the gold-coverage property -- recipe 48 had already fixed the first of the three defects #283 measured on it (`breaks_reference` now has gold-true rows in `validation` and `test`) but not the third: no row in any split has both propositions true. This check implements only the per-proposition requirement, which 48 meets, so it needed no allowlist entry; truth-combination coverage is deferred (scored-split combination coverage: 48: 3/4, 44: 11/16, 06: 13/32, 35: 14/64). Ten recipes (06, 25, 26, 31, 35, 37, 41, 42, 44, 48) are covered; an eleventh, 39, builds two propositions but is not reached by zero-argument discovery.

## Guard decision (full ruling)

**Gold-true/gold-false coverage per proposition per scored split: implemented**, with mutation proof (see "How it was verified").

**Truth-combination coverage and outcome-determining rows: deferred, not implemented**, and here is the reasoning and the cost, so this can be sequenced separately rather than guessed at:

- *Truth-combination coverage* ("at least one row for every combination the use case admits") requires knowing which combinations a given recipe's use case actually admits -- that is a judgment about the recipe's own domain (does "both true" even make sense for these two propositions?), not a fact `labels.jsonl` or the question definitions can state by themselves. A mechanical check could verify "all 2^n combinations of n propositions are present among the gold rows", but that is a stricter and different claim than "every combination the use case admits" -- it would force every recipe into full factorial coverage even where a combination is nonsensical for the task, which is exactly the kind of one-shape-fits-all guard this repository's house rules (#273's ruling, and the threshold-objective-pin check's own history) warn against adopting without evidence that the shape fits every case.
- *Outcome-determining rows* ("at least one row where each proposition's own tag changes the composed outcome") requires running the recipe's own composition function -- the `decide`-style function that turns the propositions' tags into a final action -- over the committed fixtures with each proposition flipped, and comparing outcomes. That function is not named consistently across recipes (recipe 48's is `decide_consistency`; others differ), so finding it mechanically hits the same name-vs-property problem the gold-coverage check solved by calling code instead of grepping names -- but the composition function, unlike a question builder, needs the OTHER answers as arguments (confidences, thresholds, a confidence gate), which this check cannot safely guess or default. A guard here would need either a documented naming convention for the composition entry point (which does not exist today) or a second discovery mechanism as careful as `_noul_propositions`, built and proven against the published set the same way.

Both are real, buildable guards -- I am not saying they are impossible -- but they need a design decision (what counts as "admits" for truth combinations; how a composition function is discovered without guessing its name) that is bigger than this PR's scope and that I should not make unilaterally inside a foundation PR whose diff is meant to be read in one sitting. I am handing the orchestrator a concrete starting point instead of a vague "future work" note: the outcome-determining check's hardest sub-problem is discovering the composition function without keying on a name, and the natural next step is to look for a documented convention (e.g., every recipe's composition entry point takes a `LabelDecision`-shaped or `dict[str, float]`-shaped argument) across the published set before writing a check, the same way I measured the question-builder shapes before writing this one.

## Proposed amendment text for #53 and #56

(Not applied -- I was asked to propose text only; the orchestrator applies it so the tracker keeps one voice.)

Append to each issue:

> **Fixture requirement for this recipe's `Noul` proposition(s), if more than one is asked together:** the fixture set must carry, in the split used to select each threshold, a gold-true row and a gold-false row for every proposition; at least one row for every truth combination the use case admits (both true, both false, each true alone); and at least one row where each proposition's own tag is what changes the composed outcome. The second and third are not implied by the first -- a fixture set can be positive-complete and still never exercise the states or the load-bearing-ness a battery exists to test.

## Acceptance criteria (from #283)

- [ ] "#53 and #56 carry the requirement before a builder is dispatched." **Not met by this PR** -- I propose the exact text above; I was instructed not to edit those issues myself.
- [x] "The guidance lives in a document an issue author reads." **Met** -- `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/recipe.yml`'s "Fixtures and evaluation" field now prompts for it directly.
- [x] "A decision is recorded on whether a guard enforces it, with reasons either way." **Met** -- gold-coverage is implemented and proven; truth-combination and outcome-determining coverage are ruled out of this PR's scope with the specific cost each would carry, above.

## Recipe checklist

Not applicable -- this is foundation work (`docs/`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/`, `tests/` only; no recipe folder touched).

## How it was verified

All commands run from `/workspace/worktrees/foundation-283` at head `c808be7810efb8fd69719b839ebe170336e9799c`.

```
# Verified the brief's "exact boilerplate appears in zero files" claim, can-speak proof included
git grep -n "One independent question per label or concern" -- '*'   # RC=1, no match
git grep -n "each threshold is chosen from examples and evaluated" -- '*'   # RC=1, no match
git grep -n "chosen from examples and evaluated" -- '*'   # RC=0, matches CONTRIBUTING.md:65 (can-speak proof)

# Targeted guard check, both interpreters
source .venv/bin/activate      # Python 3.14.7
python -m pytest tests/test_recipe_guard.py -rX
# -> 730 passed, 43 skipped, 49 deselected, 31 xfailed (10 passed + 40 skipped are the new check)

source .venv310/bin/activate   # Python 3.10.21
python -m pytest tests/test_recipe_guard.py -rX
# -> 730 passed, 43 skipped, 49 deselected, 31 xfailed -- identical totals

# Mutation proof the new check can both fire and not fire (fail-open discipline)
# On a scratch copy of recipes/48-document-revision-consistency/fixtures: removed every
# labels.jsonl row with breaks_reference == true, asserted the mutated text != the original
# text (mutation took), then re-ran _noul_gold_gaps on the mutated copy:
#   ORIGINAL: gaps=[]
#   MUTATED:  gaps=['validation/breaks_reference: no gold-true row (saw only [False])',
#                   'test/breaks_reference: no gold-true row (saw only [False])']
# introduces_new_fact (the untouched proposition) produced no gap in either run -- the mutation
# reddened exactly the proposition it touched, not an unrelated assertion.

# Full bare-root pytest, CI's own invocation, both interpreters, under the heavy-job lock
# (3.14, acquired as foundation-283, released by the ownership-checked trap in the same command)
python -m pytest -rX > "$TMPDIR/pytest_bare.out" 2>&1; echo $?
# -> 0; tail: "4395 passed, 46 skipped, 49 deselected, 31 xfailed in 116.85s"; grep -c
# "FAILED\|ERROR" on the full output -> 0 matches (grep rc=1, read as the three-way case:
# 0=matched, 1=clean, 2=grep itself broken)

# (3.10, same lock discipline, reacquired after the first run released it)
python -m pytest -rX > "$TMPDIR/pytest_bare_310.out" 2>&1; echo $?
# -> 0; tail: "4395 passed, 46 skipped, 49 deselected, 31 xfailed in 150.55s"; 0 FAILED/ERROR

python tools/render_catalog.py --check   # exit 0, empty output -- README unaffected (no recipe touched)
ruff check .                              # All checks passed!
ruff format --check .                     # 378 files already formatted
```

No notebook was executed locally (foundation-PR rule); no recipe file was touched; `tests/recipe_guard_known_failures.py` was not touched; no API key was used or looked for.

293.title: Sweep: prose close-out for recipes 28, 30-35, 43-45, 47, 48
293.body:
Refs #163

## What this is

A deferred prose close-out sweep across published recipes. It touches only files under `recipes/` (27 files; no shared code, no `README.md`, no catalog). It closes the following items, named individually, and nothing else:

1. **Recipe 45, two rule-15 citation rewrites only.** Recipe 45's earlier margin-rows and test-only-baseline work was reverted before this branch's final head (it is additive prose and belongs to its own issue); recipe 45 contributes only its "build notes" citation rewrites (item 2).
2. **The rule-15 plural citation batch ("build notes"):** 12 occurrences across 11 files in 7 recipes (03, 05, 19, 29, 43, 44, 45). Each now states the property instead of citing a private issue section. `git grep -i 'build notes'` over all tracked files returns nothing after this change and 12 hits at `origin/main`.
3. **Recipe 28's `v05` causal connector** and **recipes 30 to 35's Level 3 prose items** (30: 2, 31: 4, 32: 3, 33: 3, 34: 3, 35: 2).
4. **Recipe 47's locality item** (the comparison word in the `baselines` cell is derived from the sign instead of the literal `beats`) and **recipe 48's positional pointer** (`baselines-note-md` no longer claims two lines are "two lines apart").

Not in this change: recipe 45's margin-rows and test-only-baseline items; the singular "build note" spelling (a separate follow-up branch), recipe 45's remaining items, recipe 28's retrieval-miss lesson rewrite.

## How it was verified

- Scope: `git diff --raw -M origin/main...HEAD` is 27 paths under `recipes/`, all mode 100644. The diff over `src tests tools docs .github CONTRIBUTING.md pyproject.toml` is empty.
- Every touched notebook re-executed offline on 3.14 with `.github/constraints-notebooks.txt`; `check_notebook_fresh.py` reports each matches a fresh run (no number moved).

298.title: Foundation: audit actual backend calls separately from replay fixture keys
298.body:
Refs #80

## What this is

Adds an optional `AuditedBackend` wrapper (`src/jev_cookbook/accounting.py`) that counts the `decide()` calls a notebook actually makes separately from the distinct replay-fixture keys those calls resolve to, and rewrites the recipe guard's README-budget check to use it. Nothing existing changes unless a notebook opts in: no backend, recipe, fixture or notebook is modified.

Why: a recipe that decides the same state more than once (repeats, retries, comparison arms) makes more calls than the replay file has entries. The old guard compared a README's stated call count to `len(responses.json)`, which is the distinct-key count, so it could pass while the notebook made a different number of real calls (recipe 36's earlier measurement: 290 calls against 72 distinct states).

- `decide_calls`: how many times `decide()` was invoked (a call that raises counts, with `returned: false`).
- `distinct_requests`: how many unique replay keys those calls had; this is the number a fixture file can match.
- The ledger carries only the replay key and a `returned` flag: no responses, contents, credentials or timing. A request that fails replay-key validation never reaches the backend and is not counted.
- This counts logical `decide()` calls, not HTTP attempts; it is separate from the live backend's `requests_made`.
- `tests/test_recipe_guard.py`: the README-budget check now requires, for an audited notebook, "makes exactly N calls" to equal `decide_calls` and the distinct keys to equal the keys in `responses.json` exactly; an unaudited recipe keeps the old `len(responses.json)` check, and a malformed audit fails rather than falling back to it.
- Docs: `docs/backends.md`, `docs/live.md`.

## Verification

The change is one commit (originally `9b9f73b`, cherry-picked onto `main` f00f56b2 with one docstring-only conflict resolved: the commit's rewritten bullet and `main`'s `noul_proposition_gold_coverage` bullet both kept). 8 files, +782/-50, no recipe folder touched.

- Bare `pytest` 4919 passed / 46 skipped / 50 deselected / 31 xfailed on 3.10 (no SDK) and on 3.14; `tests/test_live_sdk.py` 62 passed with the SDK mocked; ruff, hygiene (569 files), `render_catalog --check`, `notebook_ci.py fixtures`, `fixtures validate --all` clean.
- All 50 published notebooks and the template re-executed offline on 3.14: every one byte-identical to its committed file (no recipe uses `AuditedBackend` yet, so no printed count moves).

## Opus review — PR #185 against issue #161

Reviewed at head `499691caea0aab629fc13f6cc96ac59100567883` (signed merge of `origin/main` `89bdd1a` over the work commit `88431b7`), in a detached worktree pinned to that SHA; `headRefOid` confirmed equal. `origin/main` is an ancestor of the head, so the head is current on `main`. `statusCheckRollup`: all 34 checks SUCCESS, including `Tests (py3.10)`, `Tests (py3.14)`, the 24 per-recipe `Notebook (…)` jobs and `Notebooks (execute)`. The diff touches exactly the five allowed paths — `docs/evaluation.md`, `src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py`, `tests/test_check_hygiene_generic_usernames.py`, `tests/test_evaluation.py`, `tools/check_hygiene.py` (1093 insertions, 19 deletions); no recipe, no notebook, no workflow, no contract file. No notebook was executed locally (CI's 24 notebook jobs are green on this head). An AST signature diff of `src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py` against `origin/main` shows **no existing signature changed and nothing removed**; the eight additions are the seven new public helpers plus the private `_hit_probability`, and all seven are in `__all__` (which was already not strictly alphabetical on `main`; the new entries sit in the same near-alphabetical positions, so that is not a regression).

My own runs, in two venvs created inside the worktree (3.14 with `.[dev,ml] -c .github/constraints-notebooks.txt`, 3.10 with `.[dev]`), no `TYPESAFE_API_KEY`, `JEV_COOKBOOK_LIVE` unset, no `.env` read, no live call: `ruff check .` clean; `ruff format --check .` — 213 files already formatted, and the seven `python` fenced blocks extracted from `docs/evaluation.md` are also format-clean; `python tools/check_hygiene.py` — passed, 307 files scanned; `python tools/render_catalog.py --check` clean; `pytest tests/test_evaluation.py tests/test_check_hygiene_generic_usernames.py` — 175 passed on **both** 3.14 and 3.10; the full suite once, in the foreground under the shared heavy-job slot with `OMP/MKL/OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=2` — **2218 passed, 3 skipped in 91.86s**. Ten mutations (one or more per new helper, `__pycache__` cleared between each, `timeout 300`) each failed only that helper's own tests, with the unmutated baseline back at 175 passed — detail under criterion evidence below. Nothing is weakened: no new ignore, exclude, skip or loosened rule anywhere in the diff. No statement about Jev's quality, latency or cost is added; the only occurrence of "cost" is "what gating it too would have cost or bought", about a counterfactual coverage number. No internal process document is cited in the docs — the `#172` and `#148`/`#155` pointers are GitHub issue references in a contributor-facing doc that already carries several of them, which is established practice here, not a recipe-facing citation.

Three of the seven deliverables are solid and verified against the merged recipes' committed fixtures. One — `outcome_curve` — does not do the job the issue asked it for, and I can show that on two merged recipes' own numbers. Details by severity.

---

# Must change

### M1 — `outcome_curve` does not reproduce the rule's own `evaluate_outcomes` numbers for the recipes it was created for

`src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py:1579` — `sel = acc_mask & (conf >= t)`.

Deliverable 5's stated purpose, from the scope-consolidation comment, is "so recipes with non-confidence branches can plot the curve that matches their numbers", and S2 in the wave-2 review asks for a sweep that "would delete five bespoke caveats". With `accepted` passed as the docstring prescribes — "whether the rule answered each example, as the rule itself decided it … exactly as `evaluate_outcomes` takes it" (`:1559`) — the intersection does the opposite for the whole family of rules that have an **unconditionally accepted** branch (recipes 11, 13, 16, 21, i.e. every recipe named in issue comments 6075633380 and 6077629651 except 14): it silently *removes* the exempt, low-confidence answers at every threshold above their confidence. I re-derived both recipes offline from their committed fixtures (no notebook executed; `select_split` + `ScriptedBackend` + the recipe's own `helpers`):

**Recipe 11** (`recipes/11-clarification-selection`, frozen gate 0.3350, test split):

| | coverage | accuracy | risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| recipe's printed `evaluate_outcomes` | 0.9474 | 0.8889 | 0.1111 |
| `outcome_curve` row at the frozen gate | 0.8947 | 0.9412 | 0.0588 |

The single item dropped is `t12-budget-wrong` — a **wrong** `no_clarification_needed` answered at confidence 0.1833, exempt from the gate by design. It is excluded from every curve row above 0.1833, so the curve reads *less risky than the rule actually is* (risk 0.0588 against the true 0.1111). That is precisely the "more flattering number" failure the new docs section at `docs/evaluation.md:316` warns about for the confidence-only view.

**Recipe 13** (`recipes/13-candidate-rewrite-selection`, frozen gate 0.2800, test split):

| | coverage | accuracy | risk |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| recipe's printed `evaluate_outcomes` | 0.8421 | 0.8750 | 0.1250 |
| recipe's printed `evaluate_selective` | 0.7895 | 0.9333 | 0.0667 |
| `outcome_curve` row at the frozen gate | 0.7895 | 0.9333 | 0.0667 |

At its own frozen gate the new curve returns `evaluate_selective`'s numbers exactly — the confidence-only view this function exists to replace. (Algebraically: for a rule of the shape `exempt | (eligible & conf >= t)`, `accepted_frozen & (conf >= t)` collapses to `conf >= t` at `t = t_frozen`.) The rule's real coverage, 0.8421, appears on the curve only at `t >= 0.2267`, *below* the frozen gate — so a recipe that plots this curve and marks its frozen gate on it contradicts its own §4 outcomes section, which is the exact trap recipe 21's review reported.

For the other shape — an unconditional **reject** branch, as in recipe 14 — the `&` is right at and above the frozen gate, but the curve still cannot loosen below it: coverage caps at the frozen accept set, so the half of the sweep a recipe uses to justify its choice of gate is dead. (On recipe 06, a pure confidence-gate rule, the same cap shows up as validation coverage topping out at 0.9368 instead of reaching 1.0000.)

One fixed mask cannot express `exempt | (eligible & conf >= t)`. The issue's original proposal (comment 6075633380) was `accepted_fn`, "or a `selective_curve` variant taking an `accepted` mask per candidate threshold" — that form works; the three-argument signature in the consolidation comment does not, under the meaning the docstring gives `accepted`. Options, in increasing order of change: (a) add a `gated` mask so the selected subset is `accepted & (~gated | conf >= t)` — exact at and above the frozen gate for both shapes, and keeps the documented three arguments; (b) take `eligible` (the gate-independent verdict) plus `exempt`, which is exact at every threshold; (c) take a callable `accepted_at(t) -> mask`. Whichever is chosen, please add a test that reproduces recipe 13's **and** recipe 11's printed `evaluate_outcomes` coverage/accuracy/risk at their frozen gates from the helper — the current `test_outcome_curve_*` set passes under the present semantics and so cannot catch this.

Not in dispute, and verified: the returned row shape is right. `SelectiveCurve` is returned unchanged, `jev_cookbook.style.plot_risk_coverage(curve, …)` plots it with no edit (I called it on recipe 13's real curve and on a synthetic curve containing a NaN risk row — no exception either time), and `test_outcome_curve_equals_selective_curve_when_accepted_is_all_true` is a true identity (I reproduced it on recipe 06's test split, where the frozen cutoff accepts all 95 pooled pairs: 26 rows identical in thresholds, coverage and accuracy). The `accepted & (confidence >= t)` semantics are also documented precisely, at `:1543-1556` and `docs/evaluation.md:271-295`; the problem is the semantics, not the description of them.

### M2 — `outcome_curve` rejects the answer objects its own docstring and the docs promise

`src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py:1557` says `confidences` may be "numbers, or Choice/Score answers (`.confidence`). For Noul see `noul_confidence`", word for word what `selective_curve:1340` says. But `:1572` calls `_floats(...)` directly instead of `_conf_inputs(...)`, so the `.confidence` extraction and the Noul guard are both missing:

```
selective_curve(correct, [ChoiceAnswer, …])            -> OK, thresholds [0.6]
outcome_curve([ChoiceAnswer, …], accepted, correct)    -> TypeError: float() argument must be
                                                          a string or a real number, not
                                                          'ChoiceAnswer'
outcome_curve([NoulAnswer, …], accepted, correct)      -> the same bare TypeError
selective_curve(correct, [NoulAnswer, …])              -> ValueError: a Noul answer has no
                                                          confidence; pass noul_confidence(noul)
```

Recipes 11, 13, 16 and 21 all hold `ChoiceAnswer` objects and build `confidence` lists from them; `[a.confidence for a in answers]` works, but the documented `[r.answer for r in results]` form does not, and the failure is a `TypeError` from inside numpy's coercion rather than this module's `ValueError` convention. Use `_conf_inputs` (or the same extraction plus the Noul guard) and add a test that passes answer objects.

### M3 — `top_k_query_accuracy` claims `recall_at_budget`'s input contract but does not implement it

`src/jev_cookbook/evaluation.py:1271` says `queries` are taken "exactly as `ndcg` and `recall_at_budget` take them", and `:1288` uses bare `_floats`. The three disagree:

```
recall_at_budget(rel, [NoulAnswer, …], 1)              -> 1.0
mean_recall_at_budget([(rel, [NoulAnswer, …])], 1)     -> 1.0
ndcg(rel, [NoulAnswer, …])                             -> TypeError (ndcg extracts .score, not .noul)
top_k_query_accuracy([(rel, [NoulAnswer, …])])         -> TypeError (extracts neither)
```

The two ranking helpers are introduced as a pair, documented side by side, and meant to be called on the *same* `queries` list to show the divergence — so a recipe whose scores are Noul or Score answers gets a number from one and a `TypeError` from the other. Either extract `.score`/`.noul` the way `recall_at_budget` does, or narrow the docstring to "numbers only" and say so in the docs table. (That `ndcg` accepts `.score` but not `.noul` while `recall_at_budget` accepts both is pre-existing and belongs to another issue; I note it below.)

### M4 — the docs say the curve pair coincides for a confidence-only rule; it does not

`docs/evaluation.md:297-315`. The two bullets define the "confidence-only view" as `selective_curve`, `select_confidence_threshold`, `evaluate_selective` and the "outcomes view" as `evaluate_outcomes`, `outcome_curve`. **"When they coincide"** then says that for a rule whose only review branch is the confidence gate, "the two views agree on every field but `threshold`". That is true of `evaluate_selective`/`evaluate_outcomes` and false of `selective_curve`/`outcome_curve`. Evidence from recipe 06, which is exactly that rule (one review branch, the confidence gate, frozen cutoff 0.1200): on its validation split the two curves have the same 30 thresholds but different coverage and accuracy, because `accepted` is `confidence >= 0.12` rather than all-True, so the intersection caps coverage at 0.9368 where `selective_curve` rises to 1.0000. The curves coincide only under the stricter condition the function's own docstring states — `accepted` all True — which on recipe 06 holds on the test split (26 identical rows) and not on validation. Please state the curve condition separately from the single-number condition; as written, the paragraph tells a multi-label recipe builder that plotting either one is equivalent, and it is not. The same sentence is repeated at `docs/evaluation.md:395-399` in the three-path section, where it *is* correctly limited to `evaluate_selective`/`evaluate_outcomes`.

### M5 — the ULP note's arithmetic is off by a factor of eight

`docs/evaluation.md:104` ("**Hand-written mirror probabilities can differ from `noul_confidence` by 1 ULP.**") and `:111` ("the results differ by 1 ULP"). The two *inputs* are 1 ULP apart — `1 - 0.42 == 0.5800000000000001` is one ULP above the literal `0.58`, and that part is exactly right. The two *results* quoted on the same line are 8 ULPs apart: `0.16000000000000014 - 0.15999999999999992 == 2.220446049250313e-16`, against `math.ulp(0.16) == 2.7755575615628914e-17`. The `0.86` pair the note alludes to ("printed twice, at a 1-ULP apart value") is 2 ULPs apart: `noul_confidence([0.07, 0.93])` is `0.8599999999999999` and `0.8600000000000001`. Everything else in the note checks out verbatim — both quoted confidences are the real values, and `selective_curve` on that mirror pair really does return two threshold rows for one nominal 0.16. In a repository whose contract is about not overstating a number, "by 1 ULP" in a heading and in a body sentence should say "by a few ULPs" (or give the 8), and the "1-ULP apart value" phrase should move to the inputs where it is true.

---

# Suggestions (not blocking)

1. **The identity tests do not run on recipe 06's committed fixtures.** `tests/test_evaluation.py` copies the two hand-rolled helpers as `_pooled_correct_and_confidence` and `_tally_outcomes` (faithfully — I diffed them against the notebook's `python-cutoff` and `evaluation-selective` cells and the only differences are `e` for `e.id` and the literal `"uncertain"` for `helpers.UNCERTAIN`) but runs them over four synthetic examples and two labels defined in the test file. I ran the real check myself and it is exact (see criterion 1 below), so this is not a correctness doubt — but a test over 4×2 invented rows will not notice if a future edit diverges on the 19×5 shape that actually exists. A `tests/test_recipe_*`-style test that loads recipe 06's fixtures would.
2. **`top_k_query_accuracy` is not the name the issue says.** The rename away from `top_k_accuracy` is the right call (the slot is taken by the Choice-distribution function, whose signature must not move) and `docs/evaluation.md:184-196` explains the distinction well. But #161's own text and anything briefed from it still say `top_k_accuracy`; worth a line on the issue so the next fifty recipes are briefed on the real name.
3. **`top_k_query_accuracy([(1, 2)])` raises `TypeError: 'int' object is not iterable`**, not the module's `ValueError`. Same root cause as M3. `mean_recall_at_budget([([1,0],[0.9,0.1],3)], 1)` raises `ValueError: too many values to unpack`, which is at least the right class but an unhelpful message.
4. **`fallback_metrics`'s `present` field.** The docs row for `ClassificationCounts` now says it is "what `fallback_metrics` returns for the fallback class"; `present` (`tp + fp + fn > 0`) is meaningful there but unmentioned, and a reader who sees `present=False` on a fixture where the fallback neither appears in gold nor is ever chosen will want the one-line gloss.
5. Issue comment 6075167730's **second** docs ask — a warning that on small fixture sets `select_confidence_threshold(target_accuracy=…)` can step straight to the bottom of the curve (recipe 17: 1.0 → 0.5600 but every target from 0.95 down → 0.0600) — is not in this PR. It was not in the seven-item consolidation list, so this is not a gap in scope; see the "still open" list.

---

# Deliverables, with my own evidence

**1. Multi-label pooling + outcome tally — MET.** I re-derived recipe 06 offline from its committed `fixtures/` with its own `helpers.py` and the scripted backend, and compared the helpers against the notebook's hand-rolled functions on the real 19×5 = 95 pooled pairs:

- `pool_label_decisions` vs `pooled_correct_and_confidence`: `correct` lists identical; `confidence` lists **bit-identical** (`==`, not `approx`); `keys` are `(example_id, label)` in label-major, example-minor order, so `keys[j]` names `correct[j]`/`confidence[j]`, and the first 19 keys are all `pricing`.
- `pool_label_outcomes` + `evaluate_outcomes` vs `tally_outcomes`: validation `total=95 answered=89 coverage=0.9368 accuracy=0.9888 risk=0.0112`; test `total=95 answered=95 coverage=1.0000 accuracy=0.9789 risk=0.0211` — identical to the recipe's committed printed output on both splits, and the recipe's frozen per-label thresholds (`pricing 0.44, reliability 0.47, usability 0.52, support 0.40, feature_request 0.82`) and cutoff `0.1200` re-derived from the fixtures.

Validation: empty `example_ids`/`labels`, missing label in any mapping, missing threshold, threshold outside [0, 1] and length mismatch all raise `ValueError`; `_noul_array` keeps the #160 [0, 1] guard on noul values; `_same_length` is used explicitly and `zip(..., strict=True)` in the reference helper. Mutations: inverting `tag == gold`, reversing the pooling order, swapping the key tuple, and using the raw noul as the confidence each failed exactly two `pool_label_decisions` tests and nothing else; forcing `accepted` all-True failed exactly the two `pool_label_outcomes` identity tests.

**2. Hygiene generic username `agent` — MET.** `whoami` in this container is literally `agent`, so the premise is real. The change is confined to `_GENERIC_USERNAMES`, which is read only by `_local_usernames()` — the running account's *own* name filter. The path rules (`linux-home-path`, `macos-home-path`, `pytest-of-…`, `windows-user-path`, …) are untouched, so a leaked `/home/agent/...` is still caught. The tests check both directions, and I confirmed the hard one myself: with `USER=agent` and `LOGNAME=quillfeather`, `_local_usernames()` is `{"quillfeather"}`, the output `hello from QUILLFEATHER!` still raises `local-username`, and `agent output follows` raises nothing; `USER=agentsmith` is still a real checkable username. Removing `agent` from the set failed four tests, including `test_a_real_username_is_still_flagged_when_agent_is_also_a_reported_name`. `python tools/check_hygiene.py` over the whole repository passes, 307 files scanned. The four speculative siblings (`task`, `worker`, `sandbox`, `service`) are not this container's names and are added on a stated analogy; they cost nothing but detection of a real account literally so named, which I accept.

**3. `noul_confidence` ULP docs note — MET apart from M5.** The quoted literals, the `1 - 0.42 == 0.5800000000000001` claim, the two confidence values and the "two adjacent threshold candidates" consequence all reproduce exactly (`selective_curve` on the mirror pair returns 2 rows for one nominal 0.16). It correctly says the code fix is out of scope and points at #172. The "1 ULP" magnitude is wrong (M5).

**4.
